arxiv-2209-08503.title: Revisiting Rolling Shutter Bundle Adjustment: Toward Accurate and Fast Solution
arxiv-2209-08503.creator: Bangyan Liao, Delin Qu, Yifei Xue, Huiqing Zhang, Yizhen Lao
arxiv-2209-08503.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Bangyan Liao, Delin Qu, Yifei Xue, Huiqing Zhang, Yizhen Lao. We propose an accurate and fast bundle adjustment (BA) solution that estimates the 6-DoF pose with an independent RS model of the camera and the geometry of the environment based on measurements from a rolling shutter (RS) camera. This tackles the challenges in the existing works, namely, relying on high frame rate video as input, restrictive assumptions on camera motion and poor efficiency.

arxiv-2306-17057.title: Field-theoretic Analysis of Directed Percolation: Three-loop Approximation
arxiv-2306-17057.creator: Loran Ts. Adzhemyan, Michal Hnatič, Ella V. Ivanova, Mikhail V. Kompaniets, Tomǎš Lučivjanský, Lukáš Mižišin
arxiv-2306-17057.description: Abstract The directed bond percolation is a paradigmatic model in non-equilibrium statistical physics. It captures essential physical information on the nature of continuous phase transition between active and absorbing states. In this paper, we study this model by means of the field-theoretic formulation with a subsequent renormalization group analysis.

arxiv-2404-16709.title: Understanding Measurement Precision from a Regression Perspective
arxiv-2404-16709.description: Abstract We adopt and expand McDonald’s (2011) regression framework for measurement precision, integrating two key perspectives: (a) reliability of observed scores and (b) optimal prediction of latent scores. Reliability arises from a measurement decomposition of an observed score into its true score and measurement error.

arxiv-2412-18874.title: IUST_PersonReId: A New Domain in Person Re-Identification Datasets Journal: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence
arxiv-2412-18874.creator: Alireza Sedighi Moghaddam, Fatemeh Anvari, Mohammadjavad Mirshekari Haghighi, Mohammadali Fakhari, Mohammad Reza Mohammadi
arxiv-2412-18874.description: Abstract Person re-identification (ReID) models often struggle to generalize across diverse cultural contexts, particularly in Islamic regions like Iran, where modest clothing styles are prevalent. Existing datasets predominantly feature Western and East Asian fashion, limiting their applicability in these settings.

arxiv-2503-19650.title: HausaNLP at SemEval-2025 Task 3: Towards a Fine-Grained Model-Aware Hallucination Detection
arxiv-2503-19650.creator: Maryam Bala, Amina Imam Abubakar, Abdulhamid Abubakar, Abdulkadir Shehu Bichi, Hafsa Kabir Ahmad, Sani Abdullahi Sani, Idris Abdulmumin, Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhamad, Ibrahim Said Ahmad
arxiv-2503-19650.description: Abstract This paper presents our findings of the Multilingual Shared Task on Hallucinations and Related Observable Overgeneration Mistakes, MU-SHROOM, which focuses on identifying hallucinations and related overgeneration errors in large language models (LLMs). The shared task involves detecting specific text spans that constitute hallucinations in the outputs generated by LLMs in 14 languages.

arxiv-2508-00314.title: Hybrid Scandium Aluminum Nitride/Silicon Nitride Integrated Photonic Circuits
arxiv-2508-00314.creator: Jiangnan Liu, Shuai Liu, Abdur-Raheem Al-Hallak, Huabin Yu, Zhengwei Ye, Yuheng Zhang, Zheshen Zhang, Zetian Mi
arxiv-2508-00314.description: Abstract Scandium doped aluminum nitride has recently emerged as a promising material for quantum photonic integrated circuits (PICs) due to its unique combination of strong second-order nonlinearity, ferroelectricity, piezoelectricity, and complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) compatibility. However, the relatively high optical loss reported to date —typically above 2.4 dB/cm—remains a key challenge that limits its widespread application in low-loss PICs.

arxiv-2509-24674.title: Advancing Zero-Shot Open-Set Speech Deepfake Source Tracing
arxiv-2509-24674.creator: Manasi Chhibber, Jagabandhu Mishra, Tomi H. Kinnunen
arxiv-2509-24674.description: Abstract We propose a novel zero-shot source tracing framework inspired by advances in speaker verification. Specifically, we adapt the SSL-AASIST system for attack classification, ensuring that the attacks used for training are disjoint from those used to form fingerprint–trial pairs.

arxiv-2512-16103.title: AIMM: An AI-Driven Multimodal Framework for Detecting Social-Media-Influenced Stock Market Manipulation
arxiv-2512-16103.description: Abstract Market manipulation now routinely originates from coordinated social media campaigns, not isolated trades. Retail investors, regulators, and brokerages need tools that connect online narratives and coordination patterns to market behavior. We present AIMM, an AI-driven framework that fuses Reddit activity, bot and coordination indicators, and OHLCV market features into a daily AIMM Manipulation Risk Score for each ticker.

pmc-11525994.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of quantitative pupillometry in assessing dynamic aerobic training intensity
pmc-11525994.creator: Junlong Dai, Xingsheng Wang, Chenchen Hang, Le An, Rui Shao, Ziren Tang
pmc-11525994.description: Sports injuries often arise from improper scheduling of exercise loads, and timely assessment of these loads is essential for minimizing injury risk. This article investigates the validity of using changes in pupillary light reflex (PLR) during dynamic aerobic training as a novel approach to evaluating exercise load. Dynamic aerobic training was conducted on a power bicycle for 15 min.

pmc-11674939.title: Unveiling the Complexity of KMT2A Rearrangements in Acute Myeloid Leukemias with Optical Genome Mapping
pmc-11674939.creator: Sandrine A. Lacoste, Vanessa Gagnon, François Béliveau, Sylvie Lavallée, Vanessa Collin, Josée Hébert
pmc-11674939.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryThe classification of acute myeloid leukemias used to diagnose and inform patient care is primarily based on the identification of specific genetic changes in patient leukemic cells. The presence of a rearrangement in the KMT2A gene is frequently associated with a poor clinical outcome, but promising treatments targeting this type of abnormality are currently being evaluated and could greatly affect patients’ outcomes. It is therefore of the utmost importance to properly identify the presence of these rearrangements in patients.

pmc-12470123.title: Genetic Diversity and Selection of MHC I-UAA in Clariid Catfish from Thailand: Implications for Breeding and Conservation
pmc-12470123.creator: Ton Huu Duc Nguyen, Piangjai Chalermwong, Chananya Patta, Wattanawan Jaito, Worapong Singchat, Thitipong Panthum, Trifan Budi, Kednapat Sriphairoj, Sittichai Hatachote, Prapansak Srisapoome, Narongrit Muangmai, Darren K Griffin, Agostinho Antunes, Prateep Duengkae, Kornsorn Srikulnath, Wenteng Xu
pmc-12470123.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: Understanding variabilities in the Major Histocompatibility Complex class I (MHC I) gene is essential for evaluating immunogenetic diversity in clariid catfish. MHC I plays a critical role in immune defense by presenting endogenous antigens to cytotoxic T cells. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the genetic diversity, selection patterns, and phylogenetic relationships of MHC I alleles in three important clariid catfish species (Clarias gariepinus, Clarias macrocephalus, and Clarias batrachus) across wild and hatchery populations in Thailand.

pmc-12773387.title: Abstract 084: Intracranial Onyx Resolute Stenting In Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension Patient With Pre‐existing Nickel Allergy: Case Report
pmc-12773387.creator: Vatsala Kapoor, Brian Tong, Dan‐Victor Giurgiutiu
pmc-12773387.description: IntroductionIdiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is a pathology involving an increase in intracranial pressure leading to symptoms including papilledema, tinnitus, and elevated cerebrospinal fluid opening pressure. Recent research has identified venous sinus stenosis as a cause of IIH, a common treatment of which is venous stenting and angioplasty.

pmc-12804991.title: CBX2 promoted oral squamous cell carcinoma via increasing CEP55/NF-κB/METTL3/SHP2 signaling induced metastasis/proliferation and angiogenesis
pmc-12804991.creator: Sai Ma, Zhonghua Wang, Chao Li, Zhenli Liu, Xuan Zhang
pmc-12804991.description: To investigate the mechanism by which CBX2 promotes oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) by increasing CEP55/NF-κB/METTL3/SHP2 signaling, leading to metastasis, proliferation, and angiogenesis. We employed a comprehensive research approach. Through bioinformatics analysis (GSE153918 dataset), we identified differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and enriched pathways associated with OSCC and CBX2.

pmc-12920587.title: Skills acquisition in cavity preparation in conservative dentistry through virtual haptic simulation
pmc-12920587.creator: Sebastiana Arroyo-Bote, Catalina Bennasar-Verger, Daniela Paz-Vallejos, Jorge Dominguez-Perez, Pere Riutord-Sbert, Thais Cristina Pereira
pmc-12920587.description: IntroductionVirtual reality-based training tools have become increasingly incorporated into health education in recent years. In dentistry, three-dimensional (3D) haptic simulators are used in several undergraduate programs to support preclinical training in procedures such as caries removal, cavity preparation, coronal access, prosthodontic preparation, periodontal therapy, and surgical techniques.

pmc-13006138.description: BackgroundOral antibiotics are effective in treating uncomplicated bloodstream infections (BSIs), but they are underused. The objective of this study was to evaluate the impact of a standardized antimicrobial stewardship intervention for early transition to oral antibiotics (“oral transition”) for patients with uncomplicated BSIs.
